extraction.Name: John Beauvais
extraction.Refused/Protested: I brought the patent in here, took it up to Joe Coursey, and told him I never applied for that patent. He said "That is given to you; take it and go on home."
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: Yes. The consideration was $2400.00. It was never mortgaged.
extraction.Buyer: Henry Anderson of Runningville, S. D. for $2400.00
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: There were not debts to be settled for at time of sale.
extraction.Occupation/Income: I've got timber land, I sell fire wood, posts, and when it's time to plant, then I farm.
extraction.NOTES: Patent mailed to Mission and Ben Beauvais took it out to him at Wood, S.D. First payment was $300.00 cash, then $50.00 cash, $50.00 cash, two tents, a hay sweep worth about $50.00, a riding plow, a team with collars for $306.00; up to date he has owed me $640.00. Has one daughter who is married; has no wife. In good health. Sworn June 24, 1929 before L. E. McKean, Superintendent.
